requirements.title: Centralized Node Management and Job Allocation Across Clusters
requirements.description: The Model Manager (MM) must manage job execution on one or more clusters by handling node allocation, management, utilization, and determining cluster job scheduling while allowing users to optionally specify a target cluster for customized jobs.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: Node allocation, management and utilization will be provided by the MM

requirements.title: Weather FDDA Model Job Setup and Submission
requirements.description: The Job-Setup module must support configuring and submitting Weather FDDA jobs (GMOD jobs, re-runs, and case studies) using standard or custom configurations including model selection (MM5 or WRF), domains, cycle time, sigma levels, IC/BC data sources, observation sources, and execution settings.
ambiguities: Defaults for a GMOD job and definitions for a standard MM5 executable are TBD.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to automate the set up of new real time and off-line FDDA jobs.

requirements.title: ClimoFDDA Job Configuration and Execution
requirements.description: The system must allow users to configure and submit ClimoFDDA climate jobs by setting parameters including domain location, pseudo-obs/cross-sections, MM5 setups, timelines, ensemble statistics options, target nodes, and output post-processing options.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

requirements.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job Execution
requirements.description: The system must support configuring and running post-processing jobs independently on specified existing model output files or output produced by running/scheduled FDDA jobs.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to only run “post-processing” on an existing model output file.

requirements.title: By-Hand Custom Job Submission
requirements.description: The system must allow users to register and run custom 'by-hand' script jobs on identified clusters by supplying mandatory job metadata including script location, run time, executable names, max runtime, and output locations.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to accommodate the current GMOD-framework.

requirements.title: Job Configuration Loading from File
requirements.description: The system must allow users to load a job configuration from a specified file, modify settings if needed, save changes, and submit the job.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

requirements.title: Saved Job Configuration Retrieval and Re-run
requirements.description: The system must allow authenticated users to retrieve previously saved job configurations, modify or delete them, and re-submit jobs.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to retrieve a previous job configuration and to re-run this job

requirements.title: Job Monitoring and Control Operations
requirements.description: The system must enable users to monitor scheduled, running, and past jobs via a job table, view detailed job logs, and allow job owners and super users to delete queued jobs, stop running jobs, restart jobs, or resume stopped jobs.
ambiguities: Job prioritization rules and exact detailed information attributes are TBD.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to facilitate monitoring of running jobs, viewing the job queue and viewing jobs that ran in the past.

requirements.title: MetVault Integration and Standalone Capability
requirements.description: The Model Manager must be capable of operating both in conjunction with MetVault (for obtaining input data or saving model output) and as a stand-alone application with no knowledge of MetVault.

source_references.excerpt: The MM can run in conjunction with the MetVault, and it can also run as a stand-alone application with no knowledge about a MetVault.

requirements.title: Automated Setup and Node Management Enhancement
requirements.description: The primary goal of extending the existing model back end system is to automate the setup, running, and monitoring of model jobs across scaling hardware and projects.

source_references.excerpt: The primary goal of this project is to extend the current model back end system and to automate the setup, running and monitoring of model jobs.

scenarios.title: Centralized Automatic Node Allocation and Scheduling Across Clusters
scenarios.objective: Verify that MM automatically manages node allocation and determines cluster job scheduling across multiple managed clusters when no target cluster is explicitly specified.
preconditions: User is logged into the Model Manager with active managed clusters available.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: Node allocation, management and utilization will be provided by the MM

scenarios.title: Customized Job Scheduling with Explicit Cluster Selection
scenarios.objective: Verify that a user can explicitly specify a target cluster for a customized job, and the MM schedules the job on the designated cluster.
preconditions: User is logged into MM and multiple clusters are registered.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: the user will need to have the option to specify what cluster his/her job should run on.

scenarios.title: Standard Weather FDDA Model Job Setup and Submission
scenarios.objective: Verify that a standard Weather FDDA GMOD job can be configured using standard parameters (MM5/WRF, domains, cycle time, IC/BC sources) and submitted successfully.
preconditions: User is logged into MM and accesses Job-Setup module for Weather FDDA.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to automate the set up of new real time and off-line FDDA jobs.

scenarios.title: Historical Cycle Off-line FDDA Prompt for Case Study or Re-run
scenarios.objective: Verify that specifying a cycle time in the past prompts the user to select whether the job is a 'case study' or 're-run'.
preconditions: User is configuring a Weather FDDA job in the Job-Setup module.

source_references.excerpt: If the cycle time is in the past, then the user is prompted to specify whether the job is a “case study” or “re-run”.

scenarios.title: ClimoFDDA Climate Job Configuration and Submission
scenarios.objective: Verify that a ClimoFDDA job can be set up with GCAT options, timeline, ensemble parameters, target nodes, and output post-processing options.
preconditions: User is logged in and selects ClimoFDDA job setup.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

scenarios.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job on Existing Model Output File
scenarios.objective: Verify that a standalone post-processing job can be configured and run independently on an existing specified output file.
preconditions: An existing model output file is present at a known location.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to only run “post-processing” on an existing model output file.

scenarios.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job Linked to Scheduled/Running FDDA Job
scenarios.objective: Verify that post-processing can be scheduled targeting output that will be generated by a running or scheduled FDDA job using JOBID and cycle time.
preconditions: An FDDA job is scheduled or actively running with a known JOBID and cycle time.

source_references.excerpt: If the model output file will be produced by a running or scheduled FDDA-job, then the user supplies JOBID & cycle time

scenarios.title: By-Hand Custom Script Job Registration and Execution
scenarios.objective: Verify that a user can register and execute a custom 'by-hand' script job by providing all required mandatory metadata.
preconditions: User has set up custom scripts on the target cluster machine.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to accommodate the current GMOD-framework.

scenarios.title: Rejection of By-Hand Job Submission with Missing Mandatory Metadata
scenarios.objective: Verify that the MM rejects a 'by-hand' job registration attempt if mandatory metadata parameters (e.g. script location or executable name) are missing.
preconditions: User opens the 'Submit a By-Hand Job' interface.

source_references.excerpt: In order for the MM to accept the job, the user will have to provide certain mandatory information about the job.

scenarios.title: Load, Modify, Save, and Submit Job Configuration from File
scenarios.objective: Verify that a user can load an existing job configuration from a specified file, modify its properties, save changes, and submit the job.
preconditions: A valid job configuration file exists on the reachable file system.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

scenarios.title: Attempt to Load Invalid or Missing Configuration File
scenarios.objective: Verify system behavior when attempting to load a non-existent or malformed job configuration file.
preconditions: User navigates to 'Submit a job configuration file' menu.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: User supplies file name to load.

scenarios.title: Retrieve, Modify, and Re-submit Previously Saved Configuration
scenarios.objective: Verify that an authenticated user can retrieve a previously saved job configuration, modify settings, and submit it as a new run.
preconditions: User is logged in and has at least one saved job configuration.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to retrieve a previous job configuration and to re-run this job

scenarios.title: Delete Saved Job Configuration
scenarios.objective: Verify that an authenticated user can select and permanently delete a previously saved job configuration from their configuration list.
preconditions: User is logged in and possesses saved job configurations.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: User selects a job. User can change or delete this job configuration.

scenarios.title: Job Monitoring Table and Log Viewing
scenarios.objective: Verify that users can view job statuses in the job table across filtering categories (running, scheduled, past, all) and view detailed log files for selected jobs.
preconditions: User is logged into MM and jobs exist in various states.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to facilitate monitoring of running jobs, viewing the job queue and viewing jobs that ran in the past.

scenarios.title: Job Lifecycle Control Operations (Stop, Restart, Resume, Delete)
scenarios.objective: Verify state transitions when stopping running jobs, resuming stopped jobs, restarting jobs, or deleting queued jobs.
preconditions: Jobs owned by the user are present in scheduled and running states.

source_references.excerpt: User can stop his/her running job.

scenarios.title: Unauthorized User Control Attempt on Non-Owned Job
scenarios.objective: Verify that a regular user cannot stop, restart, resume, or delete a job owned by another user.
preconditions: User A is logged in as a standard non-super user; User B has running/queued jobs.

source_references.excerpt: User can delete his/her jobs from the job queue. A “super user” can delete any job from the job queue.

scenarios.title: Super User Management of Arbitrary User Jobs
scenarios.objective: Verify that a logged-in super user can stop, delete, restart, or resume any job regardless of ownership.
preconditions: User is logged in with super user privileges.

source_references.excerpt: A “super user” can stop any running job.

scenarios.title: Model Manager Operation in Standalone Mode Without MetVault
scenarios.objective: Verify that MM can successfully configure, submit, and run model jobs in standalone mode without connection or dependency on MetVault.
preconditions: MM is configured and operating in standalone mode.

source_references.excerpt: The MM can run in conjunction with the MetVault, and it can also run as a stand-alone application with no knowledge about a MetVault.

scenarios.title: Model Manager Integration with MetVault Data Input and Output
scenarios.objective: Verify that when integrated with MetVault, MM retrieves input data from MetVault and can save designated model output files back to MetVault.
preconditions: MM is connected to an accessible MetVault system.

source_references.excerpt: The MM can run in conjunction with the MetVault

scenarios.title: Automated Setup, Execution, and Monitoring Backend Lifecycle
scenarios.objective: Verify complete automated end-to-end processing from automated job setup, hardware node allocation, job execution, to monitoring completion.
preconditions: MM is fully initialized with target clusters ready to run automated backend jobs.

source_references.excerpt: The primary goal of this project is to extend the current model back end system and to automate the setup, running and monitoring of model jobs.

test_cases.title: Centralized Automatic Node Allocation and Scheduling Across Clusters
preconditions: User is logged into the Model Manager with active managed clusters available.

steps.action: Log into the Model Manager web interface and open the 'Submit a New Model Job' setup menu.
steps.expected_result: The Model Job setup interface loads successfully.

steps.action: Configure job parameters (JOBID 'JOB-AUTO-01', model WRF) while leaving the target cluster selection option blank.
steps.expected_result: The parameters are accepted and target cluster selection remains unassigned/automatic.

steps.action: Submit the job and navigate to the Job Queue monitoring table.
steps.expected_result: The Model Manager evaluates node utilization, assigns the job to an active cluster, allocates nodes automatically, and starts execution.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: Node allocation, management and utilization will be provided by the MM

test_cases.title: Customized Job Scheduling with Explicit Cluster Selection
preconditions: User is logged into MM and multiple clusters are registered.

steps.action: Navigate to 'Set up a new model job' in the Model Manager interface.
steps.expected_result: Model job setup form is displayed.

steps.action: Enter JOBID 'JOB-SPEC-02' and explicitly select target cluster 'Cluster-B' from the cluster dropdown list.
steps.expected_result: 'Cluster-B' is selected as the designated execution target.

steps.action: Submit the job configuration and observe the assigned cluster in the Job Queue.
steps.expected_result: The job status displays RUNNING or SCHEDULED specifically on 'Cluster-B'.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: the user will need to have the option to specify what cluster his/her job should run on.

test_cases.title: Standard Weather FDDA Model Job Setup and Submission
preconditions: User is logged into MM and accesses Job-Setup module for Weather FDDA.

steps.action: Select 'Set up a Weather FDDA Job' in the Job-Setup module.
steps.expected_result: Weather FDDA configuration forms are presented.

steps.action: Configure JOBID 'WFDDA-01', select model 'MM5', assign pre-defined domains, set current cycle time, and choose standard ETA IC/BC data sources.
steps.expected_result: All input fields update with selected standard parameters.

steps.action: Click 'Submit' to run the Weather FDDA job.
steps.expected_result: Job 'WFDDA-01' is accepted and submitted to the backend system.

source_references.section: 3.1 Set up and submit a model job
source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to automate the set up of new real time and off-line FDDA jobs.

test_cases.title: Historical Cycle Off-line FDDA Prompt for Case Study or Re-run
preconditions: User is configuring a Weather FDDA job in the Job-Setup module.

steps.action: Begin setting up a Weather FDDA job and enter a cycle time set in the past (e.g., 2005-01-01 00:00).
steps.expected_result: System detects that the specified cycle time is historical.

steps.action: Observe the modal dialog/prompt displayed by the interface.
steps.expected_result: A prompt appears asking the user to specify whether the job is a 'case study' or 're-run'.

steps.action: Select 're-run' and complete submission.
steps.expected_result: The job is logged and processed as an off-line re-run.

source_references.excerpt: If the cycle time is in the past, then the user is prompted to specify whether the job is a “case study” or “re-run”.

test_cases.title: ClimoFDDA Climate Job Configuration and Submission
preconditions: User is logged in and selects ClimoFDDA job setup.

steps.action: Select 'Set up a Climo Job' -> 'ClimoFDDA' from the model setup menu.
steps.expected_result: ClimoFDDA setup form opens.

steps.action: Enter JOBID 'CLIMO-101', set timeline parameters (start/end time and years), choose a pre-configured MM5 setup, select hourly ensemble options, and specify 8 requested target nodes.
steps.expected_result: Parameters are populated in the form.

steps.action: Configure output post-processing options to generate NCL Plots and submit the job.
steps.expected_result: Job 'CLIMO-101' is successfully registered and queued for execution.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to integrate the GCAT functionalities within the MM.

test_cases.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job on Existing Model Output File
preconditions: An existing model output file is present at a known location.

steps.action: Navigate to 'Set up a new post-processing job'.
steps.expected_result: Post-processing setup interface is displayed.

steps.action: Select existing file input option and enter full file path '/data/output/model_out_01.nc'.
steps.expected_result: The existing output file path is validated and accepted.

steps.action: Select post-processing type 'NAPS', enter destination path '/data/post_out/', and submit.
steps.expected_result: Standalone post-processing job runs directly on the specified output file.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to only run “post-processing” on an existing model output file.

test_cases.title: Standalone Post-Processing Job Linked to Scheduled/Running FDDA Job
preconditions: An FDDA job is scheduled or actively running with a known JOBID and cycle time.

steps.action: Select 'Set up a new post-processing job'.
steps.expected_result: Post-processing setup view opens.

steps.action: Select target option for scheduled/running FDDA job and enter target JOBID 'FDDA-RUN-88' and cycle time '12:00'.
steps.expected_result: Target JOBID and cycle time fields are filled.

steps.action: Select post-processing product 'Verification', specify target destination directory, and submit job.
steps.expected_result: Post-processing job is scheduled to execute upon completion of job 'FDDA-RUN-88'.

source_references.excerpt: If the model output file will be produced by a running or scheduled FDDA-job, then the user supplies JOBID & cycle time

test_cases.title: By-Hand Custom Script Job Registration and Execution
preconditions: User has set up custom scripts on the target cluster machine.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a By-Hand Job' from the job submission menu.
steps.expected_result: By-Hand job registration form opens.

steps.action: Fill all mandatory metadata fields: Job ID 'GWDPG', Script Location 'cluster1:/scripts/run.sh', Run Time '14:00', Estimated Time '2h', Executable Name 'custom_exec', Max Runtime '02:30:00', and Output Location 'cluster1:/output/'.
steps.expected_result: All required mandatory fields are filled with valid values.

steps.action: Click 'Submit Job' and view the job in the Job Queue table.
steps.expected_result: Job 'GWDPG' is registered and appears active in the job queue table.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to accommodate the current GMOD-framework.

test_cases.title: Rejection of By-Hand Job Submission with Missing Mandatory Metadata
preconditions: User opens the 'Submit a By-Hand Job' interface.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a By-Hand Job'.
steps.expected_result: By-Hand job entry form opens.

steps.action: Enter Job ID 'HAND-INVALID' but leave mandatory fields 'Script Location' and 'Executable Name' empty.
steps.expected_result: Form contains missing mandatory fields.

steps.action: Click 'Submit Job'.
steps.expected_result: Submission is rejected with visual validation errors indicating mandatory metadata must be provided.

source_references.excerpt: In order for the MM to accept the job, the user will have to provide certain mandatory information about the job.

test_cases.title: Load, Modify, Save, and Submit Job Configuration from File
preconditions: A valid job configuration file exists on the reachable file system.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a job configuration file' and supply file path '/configs/standard_job.cfg'.
steps.expected_result: The job configuration parameters are loaded from the specified file into the interface.

steps.action: Modify the cycle interval setting to '6 hours' and click 'Save Configuration'.
steps.expected_result: The modified configuration is saved back to file/storage successfully.

steps.action: Click 'Submit Job'.
steps.expected_result: The job submits and executes using the modified configuration settings.

source_references.excerpt: The objective of this feature is to provide the ability to load a job configuration into MM from a file.

test_cases.title: Attempt to Load Invalid or Missing Configuration File
preconditions: User navigates to 'Submit a job configuration file' menu.

steps.action: Select 'Submit a job configuration file'.
steps.expected_result: File prompt field is displayed.

steps.action: Enter non-existent file path '/configs/non_existent_file.cfg' and press Load.
steps.expected_result: System displays an error message indicating the file could not be found or read.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration

test_cases.title: Retrieve, Modify, and Re-submit Previously Saved Configuration
preconditions: User is logged in and has at least one saved job configuration.

steps.action: Click 'Submit Job'.
steps.expected_result: The job re-runs using the updated configuration.

test_cases.title: Delete Saved Job Configuration
preconditions: User is logged in and possesses saved job configurations.

steps.action: Access 'Retrieve saved job configurations' list.
steps.expected_result: Saved job entries are shown.

steps.action: Select configuration entry 'SAVED-JOB-DELETE' and click 'Delete'.
steps.expected_result: Confirmation prompt appears.

steps.action: Confirm deletion.
steps.expected_result: 'SAVED-JOB-DELETE' is permanently removed from the saved job configuration table.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration

test_cases.title: Job Monitoring Table and Log Viewing
preconditions: User is logged into MM and jobs exist in various states.

steps.action: Navigate to the Monitoring & Control job table.
steps.expected_result: Job table displays options for running, scheduled, past, and all jobs.

steps.action: Filter by 'Running Jobs' and select an active job entry.
steps.expected_result: Detailed job attributes (stage, status %, assigned cluster, node count) are displayed.

steps.action: Click 'View Log Files' for the selected job.
steps.expected_result: The execution log viewer opens displaying live log outputs for the job.

source_references.section: 3.5 Retrieve and run a previously saved job configuration

test_cases.title: Job Lifecycle Control Operations (Stop, Restart, Resume, Delete)
preconditions: Jobs owned by the user are present in scheduled and running states.

steps.action: Select a running job owned by user ('MY-RUN-01') in the job table and click 'Stop'.
steps.expected_result: Job status transitions from RUNNING to STOPPED.

steps.action: Select 'MY-RUN-01' and click 'Resume'.
steps.expected_result: Job status transitions from STOPPED back to RUNNING.

steps.action: Select scheduled job 'MY-SCHED-02' in the job queue and click 'Delete'.
steps.expected_result: Job 'MY-SCHED-02' is removed from the scheduled queue.

source_references.excerpt: User can stop his/her running job.

test_cases.title: Unauthorized User Control Attempt on Non-Owned Job
preconditions: User A is logged in as a standard non-super user; User B has running/queued jobs.

steps.action: Log in as standard user 'UserA' and locate job 'USERB-JOB' owned by 'UserB' in the job queue.
steps.expected_result: Job 'USERB-JOB' is visible in the general table.

steps.action: Attempt to click 'Stop' or 'Delete' on 'USERB-JOB'.
steps.expected_result: Action buttons are disabled or system displays an authorization denial error stating only owners or super users can control jobs.

source_references.excerpt: User can delete his/her jobs from the job queue. A “super user” can delete any job from the job queue.

test_cases.title: Super User Management of Arbitrary User Jobs
preconditions: User is logged in with super user privileges.

steps.action: Log in with a 'super user' privileged account and navigate to 'All Jobs'.
steps.expected_result: Job table loads with full administrative controls.

steps.action: Select job 'OTHER-USER-JOB' owned by another user and click 'Stop'.
steps.expected_result: The running job owned by another user is stopped successfully by the super user.

source_references.excerpt: A “super user” can stop any running job.

test_cases.title: Model Manager Operation in Standalone Mode Without MetVault
preconditions: MM is configured and operating in standalone mode.

test_cases.title: Model Manager Integration with MetVault Data Input and Output

steps.action: Enable 'Save model output in MetVault' and designate output products.

test_cases.title: Automated Setup, Execution, and Monitoring Backend Lifecycle
preconditions: MM is fully initialized with target clusters ready to run automated backend jobs.

steps.action: Initiate automated model job setup with default configuration parameters via MM.
steps.expected_result: Job setup details are generated automatically.

steps.action: Submit the automated job and observe node allocation.
steps.expected_result: MM backend automatically allocates appropriate cluster hardware nodes and triggers job start.

steps.action: Monitor execution through status updates until completion.
steps.expected_result: Status updates automatically progress from SCHEDULED to RUNNING to DONE in the monitoring table.

source_references.excerpt: The primary goal of this project is to extend the current model back end system and to automate the setup, running and monitoring of model jobs.
